subject.title: gateway HTTP ingress skips browser Origin check under auth.mode none (cross-origin CSRF on state-changing routes)

question: Should Gateway HTTP reject requests with a disallowed browser `Origin` before accepting `gateway.auth.mode="none"`, while continuing to allow origin-less private-ingress clients?
rationale: This touches the Gateway auth/CSRF boundary for an explicit no-auth mode that is documented for trusted private ingress, so automation should not silently redefine that contract without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Enforce Origin for browser HTTP
options.body: Reject any HTTP request carrying a disallowed `Origin` before the none-mode success return, matching the WebSocket invariant while preserving origin-less clients.

options.title: Document none as pure no-auth
options.body: Leave current behavior intact but update docs/audit to state that mode none does not provide browser CSRF Origin protection on HTTP routes.

options.title: Add an explicit strict mode
options.body: Preserve current none-mode behavior by default and add a new opt-in strict Origin policy, accepting the added config surface and upgrade complexity.

recommendation.title: Enforce Origin for browser HTTP
recommendation.body: Reject any HTTP request carrying a disallowed `Origin` before the none-mode success return, matching the WebSocket invariant while preserving origin-less clients.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter's history is strongest across Gateway auth hardening and security-boundary decisions that define this contract.
